source.title: MetaSAEs: Joint Training with a Decomposability Penalty Produces More Atomic Sparse Autoencoder Latents

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results about the atomicity of sparse-autoencoder latents, not the claim's model-neuron poles or any of its specified versions. Its findings are adjacent and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates SAE latent co-occurrence and automated interpretability, not whether model neurons or their poles have one or more jobs. Its fuzzing evaluation is for SAE features, not neuron explanations scored by simulating their activations on new text. No claim version is tested.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse autoencoders with a meta-SAE decomposability penalty and measures SAE-latent co-occurrence and fuzzing scores on GPT-2 large and Gemma 2 9B. It never measures model neurons or their poles, InceptionV1 neurons, neuron-based attribution graphs, or simulation-scored neuron explanations. Bills et al. (2023) is cited only as a method source. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that joint training with a decomposability penalty makes SAE latents more atomic: a 7.5% |φ| reduction and 7.6% fuzzing gain on GPT-2 large at 0.6pp extra CE overhead, with directional Gemma 2 9B results. They draw no conclusions about model neurons.
record.recipe_differences: Joint training of a primary sparse autoencoder and a meta sparse autoencoder with a decomposability penalty; the paper does not test neuron-pole job counts or the claim's neuron-explanation evaluation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with λ2 and σ2: λ2 = 1.0 increases mean |φ| on GPT-2 large, while λ2 = 0.3, σ2 = 1.0 is the best reported GPT-2 large configuration. Gemma co-occurrence results are small and mixed across configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-2 large layer 20, a meta-SAE decomposability penalty (λ2=0.3, σ2=1.0) cut mean |φ| by 7.5% and raised mean fuzzing score from 0.230 to 0.248. λ2=1.0 raised |φ|. Gemma 2 9B showed directional +8.6% ΔFuzz. Selected SAE features conflating word senses were split.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint training of an SAE with a meta-SAE decomposability penalty yields modestly more atomic and more fuzzing-interpretable SAE latents, depending on penalty strength.

record.problems: The authors state that evaluation covers one layer per model. Gemma SAEs were not fully converged, and the Gemma co-occurrence scan used a smaller token budget with wide confidence intervals. The selected Gemma configuration has directional fuzzing results. Automated interpretability uses a single stated judge model.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted reconstruction-loss and CE-overhead results because they measure reconstruction cost rather than SAE-latent atomicity. Omitted firing-rate-distribution and activation-norm descriptions because they are checks or context for the reported co-occurrence result, not separate atomicity outcomes. No rows were reported for the cited results from other work.

untested.parts: All of it: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares.
All of it: neuron-pole shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts, and scale.
All of it: InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose as the shared feature, recursive generalization.
All of it: architecture, regularization and tools as causes of messy neurons, and the vision-model estimates.
All of it: neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
All of it: explanations that fit activating examples but fail to predict neuron firing.
All of it: simulation scoring of neuron explanations. The fuzzing here scores SAE latents, not neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate and T6 classification are correct; all rows rightly link to none. Mean fuzzing scores near 0.23–0.25 are for SAE latents with a Qwen2.5-72B judge. They are not neuron-explanation simulation scores, so they cannot bear on V7.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job counts and the one-job, two-related-jobs, and not-understood shares.
Neuron-pole shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or parameter scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose as a shared feature, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture, regularization, and tools as explanations for messy late-layer neurons, and the estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and whether they explain behavior without a trained replacement model.
Whether neuron explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict where the neuron fires.
Whether explanations of model neurons score well when tested by simulating activations on new text, including the claim that only a minority score well.

rows.subject: GPT-2 large
rows.size_stated: d = 1280, 36 layers; 20,456 matched SAE feature pairs
rows.operation_detail: Automated interpretability fuzzing evaluation of matched joint and solo SAE features using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-AWQ as judge.
rows.value: Joint SAE: 0.248; paired Δ = +0.0175, +7.6%; 51.6% of pairs show higher joint scores.
rows.note: This is an automated interpretability score for SAE features, not a score of model-neuron explanations.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 9B
rows.operation_detail: Jointly trained a primary SAE with a meta SAE and decomposability penalty; evaluated co-occurrence across a parameter grid.
rows.value: Effects are small and mixed across configurations; λ2 = 1.0 shows substantial +|φ| increases alongside heavy L2 overhead.
rows.uncertainty: Wide confidence intervals; scan described as underpowered.
rows.note: The paper does not give individual numerical |φ| changes for these Gemma configurations in the text.
rows.check: The paper gives no numbers for individual Gemma configurations, only 'small and mixed' effects. 'Partial' has no defined reference here, so the state can't be read.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 9B
rows.operation_detail: Automated interpretability fuzzing sweep on random SAE features for each configuration.
rows.baseline: Solo SAE comparison; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: +8.6% ΔFuzz; described as the only configuration with clearly positive ΔFuzz.
rows.note: The paper characterizes the result as directional because the SAEs were not fully converged.

rows.subject: GPT-2 large
rows.size_stated: d = 1280, 36 layers; SAE dictionary size n = 20,480
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative case study comparing features from the joint SAE and solo SAE.
rows.measure: Qualitative feature specialization; reported fuzzing scores and cross-φ values
rows.baseline: Solo feature 2827 conflates excess-degree and sentence-final additive uses (fuzz +0.727).
rows.value: Joint feature 4741 represents the excess sense (fuzz +0.681, |φ| = 0.710); feature 14213 represents the sentence-final additive sense (fuzz +0.174, |φ| = 0.799).
rows.note: A qualitative SAE-latent example; it is not evidence about model neurons.
rows.check: This is a hand-picked splitting candidate (a selection example), not an outcome rate. Its |φ| values are solo-to-joint cross-co-occurrence, not the within-SAE co-occurrence measure.
